title: Speculative affinity and atomic tool-result injection API for concurrent tool calls
author: Marisol Vega
description:
Motivation: concurrent multi-tool workflows expose two recurring production problems: (1) partial tool-result visibility when parallel calls race into the response stream, causing downstream parsers to see incomplete structured output, and (2) transient worker-level state or resource affinity that makes retries nondeterministic (e.g., tool containers with warm caches or ephemeral K-V context). This PR introduces a small API surface and runtime behavior to make parallel tool calls ergonomic and safe for production workloads.

Summary of changes: added a ToolAffinity contract and an InjectionAtomicity flag on the tool-calling API; implemented a speculative replayer in the runtime to reduce end-to-end tail latency on transient RPC failures; introduced an atomic injection phase so tool results are only visible to the LLM output stream when all concurrently invoked tool calls for a logical turn have either succeeded or exhausted their retry budget; extended the OpenAI-compatibility shim to include a stable structured envelope for tool outputs (enables downstream validators to operate on consistent JSON payloads).

Key behavioral guarantees: (1) atomic injection: tool results for a named call-group are emitted as a single structured event or a 'tool_batch_failure' event; (2) affinity window: callers can request 'call_affinity' set to {"session","request","none"} to prefer colocating related tool calls; (3) retry semantics: default is bounded speculative retry (speculative_k=1) with backoff and idempotency-awareness based on declared tool properties; (4) backpressure feedback: runtime exposes a per-request backpressure hint that client SDKs can surface as per-tool throttling signals.

Public API additions: - POST /v1/call_tool now accepts a top-level "call_group_id" and optional "call_affinity" and "injection_atomic" boolean flags. - SDKs: new CallOptions.callAffinity and CallOptions.injectionAtomic fields (TS/Python/Go). - OpenAI-compat: structured tool envelope uses "tool_batch" event with fields {"group_id","results","status","metadata"} (stable across retries).

Compatibility & migration notes: default behavior is backwards-compatible (if no call_group_id provided, behavior matches prior per-call streaming). Existing consumers that post-process streaming text should opt-in to injection_atomic=true to get strong consistency for multi-tool outputs.

Commits (high level): - spec(api): add ToolAffinity and InjectionAtomicity interfaces and examples - runtime: speculative replayer and group coordinator to implement atomic injection - runtime: affinity scheduler that prefers warm workers within an affinity window - shim/openai-compat: emit tool_batch structured events - sdk: propagate call group and affinity flags to network layer - tests: unit + integration (including new end-to-end against the sample tool harness)

Files changed (high level): src/runtime/coordinator.rs, src/runtime/speculative_replay.rs, api/openapi.yaml, shim/openai_compat/producer.py, sdk/ts/src/calls.ts, sdk/python/redwood/calls.py, docs/tooling/multi_tool_calls.md, tests/integration/multi_tool_atomic.yml, ci/pipeline.yml

Small illustrative patch snippets: - api/openapi.yaml: added parameters: {name: call_group_id, in: body, schema: string} - shim/openai_compat/producer.py: emit({"type":"tool_batch","group_id":gid,"results":results}) only after coordinator signals commit.

Testing & CI: added an integration that spins up two test tools (one slow, one flaky) and validates the LLM-visible stream contains either the full tool_batch result or a deterministic failure envelope. CI reported a flaky test initially (test_flaky_tool_handling), reran the job; after a small timing fix in coordinator the pipeline passed.

Rollout plan: feature-flagged behind runtime flag "enable_tool_grouping". Start with internal dogfood on Dedicated clusters, then beta for hosted users with SDK opt-in.

Related: ENG-2412, ENG-2460 (design docs), SUP-8893 (customer report that motivated the atomic injection behavior).

Checklist:
- [x] API spec + examples updated
- [x] Runtime coordinator implemented with feature flag
- [x] SDKs propagated flags and examples
- [x] Integration tests added
- [x] Docs and migration guide added

runtime: speculative replayer and group coordinator
review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice clean design. Two questions: can affinity lead to hotspotting on a single worker? Can we expose affinity hints rather than hard scheduling?

Marisol Vega: Answered: affinity is a soft preference; coordinator will fall back to round-robin once per-worker outstanding bytes exceed a threshold. Added scheduling unit tests to demonstrate behavior.
Priya Shah: The speculative retry looks promising but I'm worried about double-execution side effects. Do we require tool authors to declare idempotency?
Marisol Vega: Yes. Tools.yaml now has an 'idempotent' boolean and runtime will escalate non-idempotent retries to 'fail-fast' behavior; documented in the migration guide.
Liam O'Neill: Integration test flake reproduced locally; suggested increasing coordinator deadline by 200ms. Patch pushed and CI green.
Priya Shah: Approved after test fix and docs update.
CI Bot: All checks have passed.
Squash merge commit created by Marisol Vega: 'spec: tool grouping + atomic injection'
release_notes: Add call_group_id, call_affinity, and injection_atomic flags to the tool-calling API. Introduces atomic tool_batch events to the OpenAI compatibility stream; default behavior remains backward-compatible. Feature is feature-flagged and requires SDK opt-in for full guarantees.
notes_for_ops: Feature disabled by default. To enable on Dedicated, set runtime flag 'enable_tool_grouping' and ensure tools.yaml idempotent flags are accurate. Monitor metric runtime.tool_group.commit_rate and runtime.tool_group.speculative_replays.
test_plan: Unit tests + integration harness covering (1) successful parallel calls commit atomically, (2) partial failures surface deterministic failure envelope, (3) speculative retry reduces tail in 95th/99th latency histograms. CI pipeline runs full integration suite on merge.
audits: security: reviewed for injection attack surface; validated we encode and escape structured metadata
perf: load-tested with 500 concurrent call groups; no increased p95 under config defaults
